pass: rerun R1 (post AI setup/support pricing fix; chronology-legal party)
voids_previous_receipt: receipt.json is void: its party used Magearna, Iron Leaves, Weavile, Arcanine, Whimsicott and Snorlax, none of which a player who has just reached Route 103 can hold.

PIKACHU L14 @LIGHT_BALL LIGHTNING_ROD TIMID (Fake Out/Thunderbolt/Electroweb/Helping Hand) offset 2
SHROOMISH L14 @EVIOLITE EFFECT_SPORE BOLD (Spore/Leech Seed/Giga Drain/Protect) offset 2

party_summary: Growlithe / Corphish / Treecko / Mienfoo / Mudkip / Hoothoot. Chronology: the book's C01 gives the player BOTH unchosen-by-rival starters (Treecko + Mudkip here); Growlithe, Corphish and Hoothoot are Route103 land encounters (the battle's own route); Mienfoo is a Route101 land encounter. Nothing evolved (Rustboro's stone shop and every friendship line are chapters away) and nothing fished (Mom hands the Old Rod only after this battle).

driver.scope: Synthetic headless benchmark, native AI and native debug battle lifecycle. Not earned campaign play.

attempts.narrative: T1 I doubled the two leads apart - Growlithe Flare Blitz into Pikachu, Corphish Crabhammer into Torchic. Torchic Protected the lethal Adaptability Crabhammer and banked a Speed Boost, and Pikachu chose Light Ball Thunderbolt over Fake Out and one-shot the 43 HP Growlithe outright. Mienfoo replaced it. T2 Mienfoo's Fake Out flinched Pikachu (its queued Electroweb never resolved) and Corphish's Crabhammer removed it; Taillow replaced it. T3 Corphish's Aqua Jet left Taillow alive at 1 HP, Torchic's Heat Wave removed Mienfoo before its Drain Punch, Taillow's Brave Bird removed Corphish and the recoil killed Taillow. Mudkip and Hoothoot replaced them into Shroomish. T4 Mudkip's Liquidation removed Torchic and Hoothoot began chipping Shroomish with Air Slash while Shroomish drained Mudkip. T5 Superpower made contact and Effect Spore paralysed Mudkip. T6 Mudkip withdrew for Treecko and Hoothoot's fourth Air Slash finished Shroomish. 4-3 for the player.

strategy_checks.check: Pikachu uses Fake Out only on an interruptible threat, not reflexively
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 Pikachu did NOT open with Fake Out. It read a guaranteed Light Ball Thunderbolt KO on the 43 HP Growlithe and took it, denying my Flare Blitz before it moved. That is the correct read and a visible improvement over the previous pass, where it Fake Out'd reflexively and later burned a Fake Out into a Protect.

strategy_checks.check: On its second useful turn Pikachu exploits the created advantage instead of repeating Fake Out
strategy_checks.evidence: T2 Pikachu selected Electroweb on Mienfoo (speed control for its slower partner), not a second Fake Out. Mienfoo's own Fake Out flinched it first, so the move never resolved, but the choice was right.

strategy_checks.check: Lightning Rod redirects a single-target Electric move aimed at its partner
strategy_checks.evidence: Growlithe carried Wild Charge as the probe and was KOed on T1 before it acted; Pikachu died on T2. Still unverified for E0001 after two passes. A dedicated probe attempt would have to throw the fight, which the brief forbids.

strategy_checks.check: Shroomish lands Spore on a legal, powder-vulnerable target
strategy_checks.evidence: Shroomish held the field T4-T6 opposite Mudkip, a status-free non-Grass, non-Insomnia, non-Overcoat battler, and never selected Spore once. It chose Giga Drain (T4), Giga Drain (T5) and Giga Drain (T6). Same omission as the previous pass; the setup/support pricing change did not reach Spore here. Mitigating: Giga Drain was super effective on Mudkip and healed Shroomish, so the alternative was defensible - but the authored sleep line has now never fired in two independent runs.
T5 Mudkip's Superpower made contact and Mudkip was paralysed.

strategy_checks.check: Taillow is deployed as an Orb-activation finisher, not thrown out early
strategy_checks.evidence: Unlike the previous pass, the AI never withdrew a healthy battler. Taillow entered only as the forced replacement for the fainted Pikachu at the end of T2 and immediately earned its keep: T3 Brave Bird removed Corphish. Its Toxic Orb never activated only because it entered after T2's end-of-turn and died inside T3; that is timing, not a decision error. The healthy-turn-one-switch charge visibly worked: zero voluntary switches this run against one indefensible one last run.

strategy_checks.check: Torchic's Will-O-Wisp targets a physical attacker
strategy_checks.evidence: Torchic used Protect (T1), Flamethrower (T2), Heat Wave (T3), Flamethrower (T4) and never Will-O-Wisp, although Corphish (T2-T3) and Mudkip (T4) were unburned physical attackers. Each attack it chose instead did real damage or a KO-relevant chunk, so this is a weak signal rather than a defect - but combined with the Shroomish result, status moves are still losing to direct damage on this team.

strategy_checks.check: Torchic's Protect buys a real payoff
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 Protect blocked an Adaptability Life Orb Crabhammer that was lethal to a 38 HP Fire type, and Speed Boost banked a stage behind it. The single best opponent decision of the fight.

protect_ledger.payoff: Blocked a lethal super-effective Adaptability Crabhammer from Corphish and gained a Speed Boost stage behind the guard. Large payoff.

protect_ledger_note: Exactly one opponent Protect in the whole battle, and it paid. Shroomish, which also carries Protect, never used it.

ai_defects.board: Shroomish (Effect Spore, Eviolite) active opposite Mudkip, which was status-free, Water/Ground-free of any powder immunity, awake and not behind Safeguard; Hoothoot's Insomnia made it the only illegal Spore target on my side.
ai_defects.better: Spore on Mudkip on T4 removes my only remaining attacker outright and buys the Giga Drain turns for free afterwards.
ai_defects.status: STILL PRESENT after the setup-pricing change (identical omission recorded in the previous pass).

ai_improvements_observed: No healthy voluntary switch at all this run; the previous pass's indefensible T2 withdrawal of a full-HP Pikachu into a free faint did not recur. The turn-one healthy-switch charge appears to be doing its job here.
Pikachu correctly preferred a guaranteed KO to a Fake Out flinch on T1, and speed control to a repeated Fake Out on T2.
level_changes: NONE. Won on attempt 1 but with 3 of 6 player faints and a genuine 4-3 scoreline against a chronology-honest Route 101/103 party; the brief's rule for 2+ faints is keep. The previous pass's +1 on Pikachu and Taillow is retroactively validated: Pikachu at L14 now one-shots a full-HP Route 103 lead, and Taillow at L14 traded one-for-one.
cooler: Yes, in one small way: Shroomish's Protect is dead weight on a battler whose whole point is to outlast, and the Spore line has now gone unused twice. Swapping Protect for Rage Powder would make the Eviolite body an actual redirector, turning it into the partner-protecting wall the plan describes rather than a passive drainer. Recording only - no species/move/item change in this pass.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem found. All four sets materialize and all four moves were legal on every board observed.
driver_observations: When both player battlers faint in the same turn, the first `state` call listed a phantom second pending_decision entry (`b2 SPECIES_REUNICLUS` with Psychic/Focus Blast/Recover/Protect - a species that is in neither party), and a combined `act "0:switch4" "2:switch5"` was rejected. Submitting the two switches in separate `act` calls worked. Reported, not worked around in the driver.
`result` reported opponent_faints: 0 for a battle in which all four opponents fainted; player_faints was correct at 3.
